coverageContext: Complete 44-term PR-interval research score with original GWAS beta weights. Evaluation involved 1257 European-ancestry patients referred for suspected Brugada syndrome and ajmaline testing, not a general screening cohort. Baseline PR correlation was modest; the PR slope association was not significant in the full multivariable analysis (P=0.062). GA reports a genetic sum, not measured ECG milliseconds, drug response, Brugada diagnosis, medication safety or dosing advice. The separate combined Brugada clinical model's C-statistic does not validate this score alone. No prospective clinical utility or non-European transportability is established here.

Complete 26-term QRS-duration research score with original GWAS beta weights. Evaluation involved 1257 European-ancestry patients referred for suspected Brugada syndrome and ajmaline testing, not a general screening cohort. QRS associations with baseline ECG and ajmaline response were modest and do not establish individual drug toxicity or event prediction. GA reports a genetic sum, not measured ECG milliseconds, Brugada diagnosis, medication safety or dosing advice. The separate combined Brugada clinical model's C-statistic does not validate this score alone. No prospective clinical utility or non-European transportability is established here.
